chapters: And it was, after Shaul's death, and Dovid had returned from beating the Amalekim, that Dovid dwelt in Tziklag two days.

And it was on the third day, and behold, a man came from the camp, from Shaul, and his clothes were rent, and there was earth on his head. And it was, when he came to Dovid, that he fell to the ground and prostrated himself.
And Dovid said to him, "Where are you coming from?" And he said to him, "From the camp of Yisroel, I have escaped."

And Dovid said to him, "What was the situation? Tell me now." And he said, "That the people fled from the battle, and also many of the people fell and died, and also Shaul and his son Yehonatan died."
And Dovid said to the youth who told him, "How did you know that Shaul and his son Yehonatan died?"
And the youth who told him said, "I chanced to be on Mt. Gilboa, and behold, Shaul was leaning on his spear, and behold, the chariots and the leaders of the cavalry had overtaken him.
"And he turned around behind him, and he saw me and called me, and I said, 'Here I am'.
"And he said to me, 'Who are you?' And I said to him, 'I am an Amaleki.'
"And he said to me, 'Stand over me now, and put me to death, for a shudder has seized me, for as long as my life is within me..'

"And I stood over him and put him to death, for I knew that he would not live after his fall, and I took the crown which was on his head and the armlet which was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my master."
And Dovid took hold of his clothes and rent them, and likewise all the men who were with him.
And they lamented and wept and fasted until evening, for Shaul, and for Yehonatan his son, and for the people of Havayah, and for the House of Yisroel for they had fallen by the sword.
And Dovid said to the youth who told him, "From where are you?" And he said, "I am the son of an Amaleki stranger."
And Dovid said to him, "How did you not fear to stretch forth your hand to destroy Havayah's anointed?"
And Dovid called one of the youths and said, "Go near, fall upon him," and he struck him and he died.
And Dovid said to him, "Your blood be upon your head, for your mouth has testified against you, saying, "I have slain Havayah's anointed."
And Dovid lamented with this lamentation over Shaul and over Yehonatan his son.
And he said to teach the sons of Yehudah the bow. Behold it is written in the book of the just.
O beauty of Yisroel! On your high places shall lie the slain? How have the heroes fallen?
Tell it not in Gat. Announce it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Pelishtim rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.

O mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew nor rain upon you, nor shall you be fields of heave offerings, for there the shield of the mighty was rejected, Shaul's shield was as though not anointed with oil.
From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, Yehonatan's bow did not turn back, nor did Shaul's sword return empty.
Shaul and Yehonatan, his son, who were beloved and pleasant in their lifetime, and in their death they were not separated. They were swifter than eagles, and mightier than lions.
O daughters of Yisroel, weep over Shaul who dressed you in crimson with delights, who put golden ornaments on your clothes.
How did the mighty fall in the midst of the battle? Yehonatan, on your high places you were slain!
I am distressed for you, my brother Yehonatan, you were very pleasant to me. Your love was more wonderful to me than the love of women!
How have the mighty fallen and the weapons of war perished!

And it was after this, that Dovid enquired of Havayah saying, "Shall I go up into one of the cities of Yehudah?" And Havayah said to him, "Go up." Said Dovid, "Where shall I go up?" And He said, "To Chevron."
And Dovid went up there, and also his two wives, Achinoam the Yizre'elit and Avigayil the wife of Naval the Karmeli.
And his men who were with him Dovid brought up, each man and his household, and they dwelt in the cities of Chevron.
And the men of Yehudah came and there anointed Dovid as king over the house of Yehudah, and they told Dovid saying, that the men of Yavesh-Gilad buried Shaul.
And Dovid sent messengers to the men of Yavesh-Gilad and said to them, "Blessed be you to Havayah that you have performed this kindness with your master with Shaul, that you buried him.
"And now, may Havayah do with you kindness and truth, and also I shall requite you this kindness, that you have done this thing.
"And now, let your hands be strong, and be valiant, for your master Shaul is dead, and also the house of Yehudah have anointed me as king over them."
And Avner the son of Ner, the general of Shaul's army, took Ish-Boshet, Shaul's son, and brought him over to Machanayim.
And he made him king over Gilad and over the Ashurim and over Yizre'el, and over Efraim, and over Binyamin, and over all Yisroel.
Ish-Boshet, Shaul's son, was forty years old when he became king over Yisroel, and he reigned two years, but the house of Yehudah were after Dovid.
And the length of time which Dovid was king in Chevron over the house of Yehudah, was seven years and six months.
And Avner the son of Ner and the servants of Ish-Boshet the son of Shaul went out of Machanayim to Givon.
And Yoav the son of Tzeruyah and Dovid's servants went out and met together by the pool of Givon, and they sat down, these on one side of the pool and these on the other side of the pool.
And Avner said to Yoav, "Let the boys get up now and play before us," and Yoav said, "Let them get up."
And they got up and passed in number, twelve of Binyamin and of Ish-Boshet, and twelve of Dovid's servants.

And each one took hold of his fellow's head and his sword was thrust in his fellow's side, and they fell together. And he called that place 'the territory of those slain by the sharp swords' which is in Givon.
And the battle was very sore on that day and Avner and the men of Yisroel were beaten before Dovid's servants.
And the three sons of Tzeruyah were there, Yoav, and Avishai, and Asa'el. And Asa'el was as light of foot as one of the deer which are in the field.
And Asa'el pursued Avner and did not turn to go to the right or to the left from after Avner.
And Avner turned around and said, "Is that you, Asa'el?" and he said, "It is I".

And Avner said to him, "Turn you aside to your right or to your left, and take you hold of one of the boys and take to yourself his clothing." But Asa'el did not want to turn aside from following him.
And Avner continued further to say to Asa'el, "Turn you aside from following me. Why shall I strike you to the ground? And how will I hold up my face to Yoav your brother?"

And he refused to turn aside and Avner struck him with the back end of the spear under the fifth, and the spear came out from behind him and he fell there and died in his place, and it was that everyone who came to the place where Asa'el had fallen and died, stood still.
And Yoav and Avishai pursued Avner; and the sun set when they came to the hill of Ammah which is before Gi'ach by the way of the desert of Givon.
And the sons of Binyamin gathered after Avner and became one band, and they stood on top of one hill.
And Avner called Yoav and said, "Will the sword forever consume? Did you not know that it would be bitter in the end? Until when will you not say to the people to return from after their brothers?"
And Yoav said, "As Elokim lives, for had you not spoken, then from the morning the people would have gone away, each one from after his brother.
And Yoav blew the horn, and all the people stood still and pursued Yisroel no more, and they did not continue to fight.
And Avner and his men went through the plain all that night, and they crossed the Yarden and went through all the Bitron, and came to Machanayim.
And Yoav returned from after Avner and gathered all the people; and there were missing of Dovid's servants nineteen men and Asa'el.
And Dovid's servants had slain of Binyamin and of Avner's men; 360 men died.
And they carried Asa'el and buried him in his father's grave which is in Beit Lechem, and they went all night, Yoav and his men, and the light broke upon them in Chevron.
And the war between the house of Shaul and the house of Dovid was long; and Dovid kept growing stronger, while the house of Shaul were continuously growing weaker.
And sons were born to Dovid in Chevron; and his first-born was Amnon of Achinoam the Yizre'elit.
And his second, Kilav, of Avigayil the wife of Naval the Karmeli; and the third, Avshalom the son of Ma'achah the daughter of Talmai the king of Geshur.
And the fourth, Adoniyah the son of Chaggit, and the fifth, Shefatyah the son of Avital.
And the sixth, Yitream of Eglah, Dovid's wife. These were born to Dovid in Chevron.
And it was while there was war between the house of Shaul and the house of Dovid, that Avner was exerting great effort the house of Shaul.
Now Shaul had had a concubine whose name was Ritzpah the daughter of Ayah; and he said to Avner, "Why did you go in to my father's concubine?"

And Avner became very angry at the words of Ish-Boshet; and he said, "Am I the head of the dogs which belong to Yehudah? Shall I do kindness today with the house of Shaul your father, to his brothers, and to his friends and I have not delivered you into Dovid's hand? And you charge me today with the guilt concerning the woman?
"Elokim do so to Avner and so may He continue to him, for as Havayah has sworn to Dovid, for so shall I do to him.
To transfer the kingdom from the house of Shaul and to set up the throne of Dovid over Yisroel and over Yehudah, from Dan to Be'er Sheva."
And he could not answer Avner another word because of his fear of him.
And Avner sent messengers to Dovid from his place, saying. "To whom the land belongs," saying, "Make your covenant with me, and behold, my hand is with you to bring around all Yisroel to you."
And he said, "Good; I shall make a covenant with you, but one thing I ask of you, namely that you shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal, Shaul's daughter when you come to see my face."
And Dovid sent messengers to Ish-Boshet the son of Shaul, saying, "Give my wife Michal whom I espoused to myself with one hundred foreskins of Pelishtim."
And Ish-Boshet sent and took her from a man, from Paltiel the son of Layish.
And her husband went with her, walking and weeping after her up to Bachurim; and Avner said to him, "Go, return," and he returned.
And the word of Avner had been with the elders of Yisroel, saying, "In times past you were seeking Dovid as king over you.
"And now, do it, for Elokim said about Dovid, saying, "By the hand of My bondsman Dovid shall I deliver My people Yisroel from the hand of the Pelishtim and from the hand of all their enemies."
And Avner spoke also in the ears of Binyamin, and Avner also went to speak in Dovid's ears in Chevron all that pleased Yisroel and the entire house of Binyamin.
And Avner came to Dovid to Chevron, and with him were twenty men, and Dovid made a feast for Avner and for the men who were with him.

And Avner said to Dovid, "I shall get up and go and gather all Yisroel to my master the king, and they will make a covenant with you, and you will reign over all that your soul desires. " And Dovid sent Avner off and he went in peace.
And behold Dovid's servants and Yoav came from a troop, and they brought much plunder with them. Now Avner was not with Dovid, for he had sent him off and he had gone in peace.
And Yoav and all the army which were with him came and they told Yoav saying, "Avner the son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him off and he went in peace."
And Yoav came to the king and said, "What have you done? Behold, Avner came to you. Why have you sent him off, so that he has gone?
"You know Avner the son of Ner, that he has come to entice you and to know your going out and your coming in and to know all that you are doing."
And Yoav departed from Dovid, and he sent messengers after Avner, and they brought him back from the well of the thorns, and Dovid did not know.

And Avner returned to Chevron, and Yoav caused him to turn aside unwittingly into the midst of the gate to speak with him and he struck him there the fifth rib, and he died for the blood of Asa'el his brother.
And Dovid heard afterward, and he said, "I and my kingdom are innocent before Havayah forever, of the blood of Avner the son of Ner.

"May it rest upon the head of Yoav and upon all his father's house, and may there not fail from the house of Yoav one who has an issue or one who is smitten with 'zaraath', or one who leans on a staff or who falls by the sword, or who lacks bread."
Now, Yoav and Avishai his brother slew Avner because he put Asa'el their brother to death in Givon in the battle.
And Dovid said to all the people who were with him, "Rend your clothes and gird yourselves with sackcloth, and wail before Avner." And King Dovid went after the bier.
And they buried Avner in Chevron, and the king raised his voice and wept on Avner's grave, and all the people wept.
And the king lamented Avner and said, "Should Avner die like a wicked man?"
"Your hands were not bound, and your feet were not put into copper chains. As one who falls before wicked men you have fallen." And all the people continued to weep over him.
And all the people came to serve Dovid bread while it was still daytime, but Dovid swore saying, "Elokim do so to me, and so continue, if before sunset I taste bread or anything."
And all the people recognized, and it was pleasing in their eyes. All which the king did was pleasing in the eyes of all the people.
And all the people and all Yisroel knew on that day that it was not of the king to put to death Avner the son of Ner.
And the king said to his servants, "Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen this day in Yisroel?
"And today I am tender and just anointed king, and these men, the sons of Tzeruyah are harder than me. May Havayah requite the evil-doer according to his evil."
And Shaul's son heard that Avner had died in Chevron, and his hands became feeble, and all Yisroel were dismayed.

And Shaul's son had two men, the heads of troops. The name of one was Ba'anah and the name of the second was Rechab, the sons of Rimmon the Be'eroti, of the sons of Binyamin, (for Be'erot was also counted to Binyamin.
And the Be'erotim fled to Gittaim and they were living there until this day).

And Yehonatan, the son of Shaul had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the news of Shaul and Yehonatan came from Yizre'el, and his nurse carried him and fled; and it was in her haste to flee, that he fell and became lame, and his name was Mefiboshet.
And the sons of Rimmon the Be'eroti, Rechab and Ba'anah, went, and came in the heat of the day to the house of Ish-Boshet, when he was taking his midday rest.
And they came inside the house buyers of wheat, and they struck him under the fifth rib, and Rechab and Ba'anah his brother escaped.

And they came into the house and he was lying on his bed in his bedroom, and they struck him and put him to death, and they removed his head, and they took his head and went by way of the plain all night.

And they brought the head of Ish-Boshet to Dovid to Chevron, and they said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-Boshet, the son of Shaul your enemy, who sought your life. And Havayah has granted my master the king vengeance this day of Shaul and of his seed."
And Dovid answered Rechab and Ba'anah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Be'eroti and said to them, "As Havayah lives, Who delivered my person from every distress.
That he who told me saying, 'Behold, Shaul is dead,' and he was in his own eyes as a herald of good tidings, I took hold of him and slew him in Ziglag, who me to give him a reward for good tidings.
'How much more when wicked men have slain an innocent man in his own house on his bed. And now, shall I not hold you accountable for his blood, and remove you from the earth?"

And Dovid commanded the young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and feet, and hanged them up beside the pool in Chevron. But the head of Ish-Boshet they took and buried in the grave of Avner in Chevron.
And all the tribes of Yisroel came to Dovid to Chevron, and spoke, saying: "Here we are. We are your bone and your flesh.

Also, in times past, when Shaul was king over us, it was you who led Yisroel out and brought them in, and Havayah said to you, you shall shepherd my nation Yisroel, and you shall be a ruler over Yisroel.
And all the elders of Yisroel came to the king to Chevron, and King Dovid enacted a covenant for them in Chevron before Havayah, and they anointed Dovid as King over Yisroel.
Thirty years old was Dovid when he became king, and forty years did he reign.
In Chevron he reigned over Yehudah seven years and six months; and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty three years over all Yisroel and Yehudah.

And the king and his men went to Yerushalayim to the Yevusi, the inhabitants of the land, who spoke to Dovid, saying: 'you shall not come here unless you remove the blind and the lame'; as if to say: 'Dovid shall not come here.'
And Dovid conquered the stronghold of Tziyon which is the city of Dovid.

And Dovid said on that day; "Whoever smites the Yevusim and reaches the tower, and the lame and the blind, despised by the soul of Dovid." Therefore they say; "The blind and the lame shall not come into the house."
And Dovid dwelt in the stronghold and he called it the city of Dovid. And Dovid built round about from the mound and inward.
And Dovid grew steadily greater, and Havayah Elokim of Hosts with him.
And Chiram, King of Tzor, sent messengers to Dovid, and cedar-trees, and carpenters, and stone-masons of a wall, and they built a house for Dovid.
And Dovid perceived that Havayah had established him as king over Yisroel, and that He had exalted his kingdom for the sake of His people Yisroel.
And Dovid took more concubines and wives from Yerushalayim after his coming from Chevron. And there were born to Dovid more sons and daughters.
And these are the names of those that were born unto him in Yerushalayim: Shammua, and Shobav, and Natan, and Shlomo.
And Yivchar, and Elishua, and Nefeg, and Yafia.
And Elishama, and Elyada, and Elifelet.
And the Pelishtim heard that they anointed Dovid as king over Yisroel, and all the Pelishtim went up to seek Dovid; and Dovid heard and went down to the stronghold.
And the Pelishtim came and spread out in the valley of Refaim.

And Dovid inquired of Havayah saying: 'Shall I go up to the Pelishtim? Will you deliver them into my hand?' And Havayah said unto Dovid: 'Go up; for I will surely deliver the Pelishtim into your hand.'

And Dovid came to Baal-Peratzim, and Dovid smote them there; and he said: 'Havayah has broken mine enemies before me, like the breach of waters.' Therefore he called the name of that place Baal-Peratzim.
And they forsook there their images, and Dovid and his men burned them.
And the Pelishtim came up once again and spread out in the valley of Refaim.
And Dovid inquired of Havayah, and He said: 'Do not go up; circle in back of them, and come upon them from against the mulberry trees.
And it shall be, when you hear the sound of steps in the tops of the mulberry trees, then you shall bestir yourself; for then Havayah has gone out before you to smite the camp of the Pelishtim.'
And Dovid did so, as Havayah commanded him, and he smote the Pelishtim from Geva until you come to Gezer.
And Dovid continued all the chosen of Yisroel, thirty thousand.

And Dovid arose and went with all the people that were with him, from Ba'alei-Yehudah, to bring up from there the ark of Elokim, which is called a name, the name of Havayah of Hosts who dwell upon the cherubim upon it.
And they set the ark of Elokim upon a new cart, and they carried it from the house of Avinadav that was on the hill; and Uzah and Achyo, the sons of Avinadav, drove the new cart.
And they brought it out of the house of Avinadav, which was on the hill, with the ark of Elokim, and Achyo went before the ark.
And Dovid and all the house of Yisroel made merry with all cypress wood, and with harps, and with psalteries, and with timbrels, and with sistra, and with cymbals.
And they came to Goren-Nachon, and Uzah put forth to the ark of Elokim, and grasped hold of it, for the oxen swayed it.
And the anger of Havayah was kindled against Uzah; and Elokim struck him down there for his error; and there he died by the ark of Elokim.
And Dovid was angered, because Havayah had made a breach upon Uzah; and he called that place Peretz-Uzah, unto this day.
And Dovid was afraid of Havayah that day; and he said: 'How can the ark of Havayah come to me?'
And Dovid did not want to remove unto him the ark of Havayah, into the city of Dovid; and Dovid took it aside to the house of Oved-Edom the Gitti.
And the ark of Havayah dwelled in the house of Oved-Edom the Gitti three months; and Havayah blessed Oved-Edom, and all his household.

And it was told to King Dovid saying: 'Havayah has blessed the house of Oved-Edom, and all that belongs to him, because of the ark of Havayah. And Dovid went and brought up the ark of Elokim from the house of Oved-Edom into the city of Dovid with joy.
And it was when the bearers of the ark of Elokim had trodden six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
And Dovid danced with all his might before Havayah; and Dovid was girded with a linen ephod.
And Dovid and all the house of Yisroel brought up the ark of Havayah with shouting and with the sound of shofar.
And the ark of Havayah came the city of Dovid, Michal the daughter of Shaul peered through the window, and she saw the king Dovid hopping and dancing before Havayah; and she loathed him in her heart.
And they brought the ark of Havayah, and they set it in its place, inside the tent that Dovid had pitched for it; and Dovid offered burnt-offerings before Havayah and peace-offerings.
And Dovid finished offering the burnt-offering and the peace-offerings, and he blessed the people in the name of Havayah of Hosts.

And he distributed to all the people, to the whole multitude of Yisroel, both to men and women, to each individual a loaf of bread, and a portion of meat, and a barrel of wine. And all the people departed, every one to his home.

And Dovid returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Shaul came out to meet Dovid, and she said, "How honored was today the king of Yisroel, who exposed himself today in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as would expose himself one of the idlers."

And Dovid said unto Michal; "Before Havayah, who chose me above your father, and above all his house, to appoint me prince over the people of Havayah, over Yisroel; therefore I have made merry before Havayah.
And if I be demeaned more than this, and be abashed in mine own eyes, of the maidservants of which you have spoken, with them will I get me honor."
And Michal the daughter of Shaul had no child until the day of her death.
And it came to pass, when the king dwelt in his house, and Havayah had given him rest round about from all his enemies.
That the king said unto Natan the prophet; "See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of Elokim dwells within the curtains."
And Natan said to the king; "All that is in your heart go do; for Havayah is with you."
And it came to pass on the same night, that the word of Elokim was to Natan saying:
"Go and say to My servant, to Dovid; so Havayah says: 'Shall you build Me a house for My dwelling?
For I have not dwelt in a house from the day that I brought up the children of Yisroel out of Mitzrayim, to this day, but have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle.

In all wherein I have walked with all the children of Yisroel, did I speak a word with any of the rulers of Yisroel whom I commanded to shepherd My people Yisroel, saying: 'Why do you not build for Me a house of cedar?'
And now, so shall you say to My servant, to Dovid; 'Thus Havayah says of Hosts. I took you from the sheep cote, from following the sheep, to be a leader over My people Yisroel.
And I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you, and have made for you a great name, like the name of the great ones that are in the earth.

And I will appoint a place for My people, for Yisroel, and I will plant them, and they will dwell in their own place, and be disturbed no more; and the wicked people shall not continue to afflict them as formerly.
And even from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Yisroel; and I will give you rest from all your enemies. And Havayah has told you that Havayah will make for you a house.
When your days are finished and you shall lie with your forefathers, then I will raise up your seed that shall proceed from your body after you, and I will establish his kingdom.
He shall build a house for My name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
I will be to him a father, and he shall be to Me a son; so that when he goes astray I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the sons of Adam.
But My mercy shall not depart from him as I withdrew it from Shaul, whom I removed from before you.
And your house and your kingdom shall be confirmed forever before you; your throne shall be established forever."
According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Natan speak to Dovid.
And the king Dovid went in and sat before Havayah; and he said: "Who am I, O' Havayah Elokim, and what is my house, that You have brought me thus far?
As though this was yet too small a thing in Your eyes, O' Havayah Elokim: but You also spoke of Your servant's house from afar; now is this the manner of man, O' Havayah Elokim?
And what more can Dovid say to You? For You know Your servant, O' Havayah Elokim.
For the sake of Your word, and according to Your own heart, have you brought about all this greatness, to make Your servant know it.
Therefore You are great, O' Havayah Elokim: for there is none like You, neither is there any Elokim beside You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

And who is like Your people, like Yisroel, one nation in the world, whom Elokim went to redeem for Himself as a people, and to make Him a name, also to accomplish for you the greatness and fearful things for Your land, from before Your people, whom You did redeem for Yourself out of Mitzrayim, nations and their deities?
And You did establish to Yourself Your people Yisroel to be a people unto You forever; and You, Havayah, became their Elokim.
And now, O' Havayah Elokim, the word that You have spoken concerning Your servant and concerning his house, confirm it forever, and do as You have spoken.
And let Your name be magnified forever, that it may be said: 'Havayah of Hosts is Elokim over Yisroel; and the house of Your servant Dovid shall be established before You.
For You, O' Havayah of Hosts, Elokim of Yisroel have revealed to Your servant's ear saying: 'A house I will build you'; therefore has Your servant found in his heart to pray unto You this prayer.
And now, O Havayah Elokim, You are Elokim, and Your words are truth, and You have spoken unto Your servant this good thing.

And now let it please You to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You; for You, O' Havayah Elokim, has spoken it, and through Your blessing let be blessed the house of Your servant forever."
And it came to pass after this, that Dovid smote the Pelishtim and he subdued them; and Dovid took Meteg-Ammah from the hands of the Pelishtim.

And he smote Moav, and measured them off with a line, making them lie down on the ground; and he measured two cord-lengths to put to death, and one full cord-length to keep alive. And the Moavim became as servants to Dovid, bringing presents.
And Dovid smote Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Tzovah, as he went to extend his dominion to the Perat River.
And Dovid captured from him, one thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen; and Dovid houghed all the chariots and left over of them for a hundred chariots.
And Aram of Damesek came to aid Hadadezer, king of Tzovah; and Dovid smote of Aram, twenty-two thousand men.
And Dovid placed governors in Aram of Damesek; and the Aramim became servants to Dovid, paying tribute to him. And Havayah helped Dovid wherever he went.
And Dovid took the quivers of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Yerushalayim.
And from Betach, and from Berotai, the cities of Hadadezer, King Dovid took huge quantities of copper.
And To'i, the king of Chamat heard that Dovid had defeated all the army of Hadadezer.

And To'i sent Yoram, his son, to King Dovid to greet him and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and defeated him: for Hadadezer had been To'i's opponent in war, and in his possession were vessels of silver and vessels of gold and vessels of copper.
These also the king Dovid dedicated to Havayah, with the silver and the gold that he dedicated from all the nations that he had conquered.
From Aram, and from Moav, and from the children of Amon, and from the Pelishtim, and from Amalek, and from the spoils of Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Tzovah.
And Dovid made for himself a name when he returned from smiting the Aramim in the Valley of Salt, eighteen thousand men.
And he placed governors in Edom; throughout all of Edom he placed governors, and all of Edom became servants to Dovid. And Havayah saved Dovid wherever he went.
And Dovid reigned over all Yisroel; and Dovid administered justice and charity for all his people.
And Yoav the son of Zeruyah was over the host; and Yehoshafat the son of Achilud was recorder.
And Tzadok the son of Achituv, and Achimelech the son of Evyatar were priests; and Serayah was scribe.
And Benayahu the son of Yehoyada the archers and the slingers; and Dovid's sons were chief officers.
And Dovid said: "Is there yet anyone who is left of the house of Shaul, that I may do kindness to him for the sake of Yehonatan?"
And to the house of Shaul a servant whose name was Tziva, and they called him to Dovid; and the king said to him: 'Are you Tziva?' And he said: "Your servant,."
And the king said: "Is there none from the house of Shaul, that I may do to him the kindness of Elokim?" And Tziva said to the king; "There is still a son to Yehonatan, who is lame on his feet."
And the king said to him: 'Where is he?' And Tziva said to the king; 'Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Amiel in Lo-Debar.'
And king Dovid sent, and he fetched him out of the house of Machir the son of Amiel from Lo-Devar.
And Mefiboshet, the son of Yehonatan, the son of Shaul, came to Dovid, and he fell on his face, and he prostrated himself. And Dovid said: 'Mefiboshet!' And he answered: 'Behold your servant.'

And Dovid said to him: "Do not fear for I will surely show you kindness for the sake of Yehonatan your father, and I will restore to you all the land of Shaul your father; and you shall eat bread at my table continually."
And he bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you should turn towards such a dead dog as I am?"
And the king called Tziva, Shaul's servant, and said to him: 'All that belonged to Shaul and to all his household have I given to your master's son.

And you shall till the soil for him, you, and your sons, and your servants; and you shall bring so that there your master's son will have bread, that he may eat it; and Mefiboshet your master's son, shall eat bread continually at my table." Now Tziva had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
And Tziva said to the king; "According to all that my master, the king, commands his servant, so shall your servant do. As for Mefiboshet, he shall eat at my table as one of the king's sons."
And Mefiboshet had a small son whose name was Michah. And all the inhabitants of Tziva's house were servants to Mefiboshet.
And Mefiboshet dwelt in Yerushalayim; for he ate continually at the king's table; and he was lame on both his feet.
And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Amon died, and Chanun his son reigned in his stead.

And Dovid said: "I shall show kindness to Chanun the son of Nachash, just as his father showed me kindness. And Dovid sent to comfort him through his servants, for his father. And Dovid's servants came into the land of the children of Amon.

And the princes of the children of Amon said to Chanun their master: "Do you think that Dovid honors your father that he sent you comforters? Is it not in order to investigate the city and to spy it out, and to search it that Dovid has sent his servants to you?"
And Chanun took Dovid's servants and he shaved off a half of their beards, and he cut off their garments in half up to their buttocks, and he sent them away.
And they told it to Dovid; and he sent to meet them; for the men were very much ashamed. And the king said: 'Remain seated in Yericho until your beards grow, and then you shall return.'

And the children of Amon saw that they had become odious to Dovid; and the children of Amon sent and hired the Aramim of Beit-Rechov, and the Aramim of Tzovah, twenty thousand footsoldiers, and the king of Ma'achah, a thousand men, and Ish-Tov, twelve thousand men.
And Dovid heard, and he sent Yoav, and the entire host of the mighty warriors.
And the children of Amon came out, and they prepared the battle at the entrance of the gate; and the Aramim of Tzovah, and Rehob, and Ish-Tov, and Ma'achah, were by themselves in the field.
And Yoav saw that the battle front was before and behind him: and he chose of all the choice of Yisroel and he sent them against the Aramim.
And the rest of the people he gave over to Avishai his brother, and he set against the children of Amon.
And he said: "If the Aramim will be too strong for me, then you shall help me, and if the children of Amon will be too strong for you, then I shall go to your aid.
Be strong, and let us strengthen ourselves on behalf of our people, and on behalf of the cities of our Elokim: and may Elokim do what is good in His eyes."
And Yoav and the people that were with him drew forward to do battle against the Aramim, and they fled before him.
And the children of Amon saw that the Aramim had fled, then they fled from before Avishai, and they came to the city. And Yoav returned from the children of Amon and came to Yerushalayim.
And the Aramim saw that they were smitten before Yisroel, and they gathered themselves together.
And Hadadezer sent, and brought out the Aramim that were from beyond the River; and they came to Helam, and Shovach the captain of the host of Hadadezer, before them.
And it was told to Dovid; and he gathered together all Yisroel, and he crossed the Yarden, and came to Helam. And the Aramim set themselves against Dovid, and fought with him.
And the Aramim fled before Yisroel; and Dovid slew of the Aramim, seven hundred chariots, and forty-thousand horsemen, and Shovach the captain of his host he smote, and he died there.
And all the kings, the servants of Hadadezer saw that they were smitten before Yisroel, and they made peace with Yisroel and served them. And the Aramim feared to aid the children of Amon any more.

And it was, at the return of the year, at the time of the going out of kings, and Dovid sent Yoav and his servants with him, and all Yisroel; and they destroyed the children of Amon, and beseiged Rabbah. But Dovid stayed in Yerushalayim.
And it came to pass, at the time of evening, that Dovid arose from his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king's house, and he saw a woman bathing, from the roof; and the woman was very beautiful.
And Dovid sent, and inquired about the woman. And he said: 'Is this not Bat-Sheva, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriyah the Chitti?'
And Dovid sent messengers, and he took her and she came to him and he lay with her: and she was purified from her uncleanliness; and she returned to her house.
And the woman conceived; and she sent, and she told Dovid, and she said: "I am pregnant."
And Dovid sent to Yoav, "Send me Uriyah the Chitti." And Yoav sent Uriyah to Dovid.
And Uriyah came to him, and Dovid inquired concerning the welfare of Yoav, and the peace of the people, and the welfare of the war.
And Dovid said to Uriyah: "Go down to your house, and wash your feet." And Uriyah departed from the king's house, and there followed him the king's food.
And Uriyah slept at the entrance of the king's house with all the servants of his master, and did not go down to his house.
And they told Dovid saying: "Uriyah did not go down to his house. " And Dovid said to Uriyah, "Have you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?"

And Uriyah said to Dovid: "The ark and Yisroel and Yehudah dwell in booths, and my master Yoav and the servants of my master are encamped in the open field; and shall I come to my house to eat and to drink and to live with my wife? By your life and by the life of my soul, if I will do this thing."
And Dovid said to Uriyah: "Remain here today also, and tomorrow I will send you off." And Uriyah stayed in Yerushalayim that day and the morrow.

And Dovid called him, and he ate before him, and he drank, and he made him drunk; and he went out in the evening to lie on his bed with the servants of his master, but to his house he did not go down.
And it came to pass, in the morning, that Dovid wrote a letter to Yoav, and he sent it by the hand of Uriyah.
And he wrote in the letter saying: "Place Uriyah at the forefront of the fiercest battle, and go away from him, so that he will be hit and will die."
And it came to pass, when Yoav kept watch upon the city that he assigned Uriyah to the place where he knew that there were valiant men.
And the men of the city went out, and fought with Yoav and some of the people of the servants of Dovid fell; and Uriyah the Chitti also died.
And Yoav sent and told Dovid all the facts concerning the war.
And he charged the messenger saying: 'When you have finished telling the king all the facts concerning the war.
And it shall be if the king's anger is aroused, and he says to you: "Why did you approach the city to wage battle? Did you not know that they would shoot from upon the wall?

Who smote Avimelech the son of Yerubeshet? Did not a woman throw an upper millstone upon him from upon the wall, and he died at Tevetz? Why did you approach the wall?" And you shall say: "Also your servant Uriyah the Chitti is dead".
And the messenger went, and he came and told Dovid all that Yoav had sent him for.
And the messenger said to Dovid, "When the men prevailed over us and came out against us to the field, then we came upon them as far as the entrance of the gate.
And the shooters shot at your servants from upon the wall, and some of the king's servants died, and also your servant Uriyah the Chitti is dead."

And Dovid said to the messenger, "So shall you say to Yoav; Let not this thing displease you, for the sword devours many time this number; strengthen your battle against the city, and destroy it, and encourage him."
And the wife of Uriyah the Chitti heard that Uriyah her husband was dead, and she mourned over her husband.
And the mourning passed, and Dovid sent and gathered her to his house. And she became his wife, and she bore him a son. And the thing that Dovid did was displeasing to Havayah.
And Havayah sent Natan to Dovid. And he came to him and said to him: "There were two men in one city, one rich, and one poor.
The rich man had very many flocks and herds.

But the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb which he had bought and reared; and it grew up together with him and his sons; of his bread it would eat, and from his cup it would drink, and in his bosom it would lie, and it was to him like a daughter.

And there came a wayfarer to the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd to prepare for the guest that had come to him, and he took the poor man's lamb, and prepared it for the man that had come to him."
And Dovid became very angry at the man; and he said to Natan: "As Havayah lives, the man who has done this is liable to death.
And the ewe lamb he shall repay fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity."
And Natan said to Dovid, "You are the man. So Havayah says, Elokim of Yisroel: 'I anointed you as king over Yisroel, and I delivered you from the hand of Shaul.

And I gave you the house of your master and your master's wives in your midst, and I gave you the house of Yisroel and of Yehudah; and if that were too little, then would I add unto you like them and like them.

Why have you despised the word of Havayah, to do what is evil in His eyes? You have smitten Uriyah the Chitti with the sword and you have taken his wife for yourself as a wife, and you have slain him with the sword of the children of Amon.
And now, the sword shall never depart from your household for ever because you have despised Me and you have taken the wife of Uriyah the Chitti to be your wife.

So Havayah says: "Behold I will raise up against you evil out of your own house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and I will give them to your friend, and he will lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.
For you have acted in secrecy, but I will do this thing before all Yisroel and before the sun."
And Dovid said to Natan: "I have sinned against Havayah." And Natan said to Dovid, "Also Havayah has removed your sin; you shall not die.
Nevertheless, because you have greatly blasphemed the enemies of Havayah by this thing, the child also that is born to you shall surely die."
And Natan departed to his house. And Havayah struck the child that Uriyah's wife bore to Dovid, and it became mortally ill.
And Dovid besought Elokim on behalf of the child; and Dovid fasted a fast, and he came in and slept lying on the ground.
And the elders of his house stood over him to raise him up from the ground; but he would not; neither did he eat bread with them.

And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of Dovid feared to tell him that the child was dead; for they said, "Behold, while the child was yet alive we spoke to him and he did not hearken to our voices; how then shall we tell him that the child is dead, so that he do harm?"
And Dovid saw that his servants were whispering and he understood that the child was dead; and Dovid said to his servants, "Is the child dead?" And they said " dead."

And Dovid got up from the ground, and washed, and anointed himself, and changed his clothes; and he came to the House of Havayah and kneeled; and he came to his house, and he asked and they set bread before him, and he ate.
And his servants said to him: "What is this thing that you have done? For the live child you fasted and wept, but when the child died, you got up and ate bread?"
And he said, "While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, 'Who knows? Perhaps Havayah will be gracious to me, and the child will live.
But now he is dead, why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he will not return to me."
And Dovid comforted Bat-Sheva his wife, and he came to her, and he lay with her: and she bore a son, and she called his name Shlomo; and Havayah loved him.
And He sent by the hand of Natan the prophet, and he called his name Yedidyah for Havayah's sake.
And Yoav fought against Rabbah of the children of Amon, and captured the royal city.
And Yoav sent messengers to Dovid and said "I have fought against Rabbah, I have also captured the city of waters.
And now gather the rest of the people, and encamp against the city and capture it, lest I capture the city, and my name be called upon it."
And Dovid gathered all the people, and he went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and captured it.
And he took the crown of Malkam off his head; and its weight was a talent of gold, and a precious stone; and it was on Dovid's head. And the spoil of the city he brought forth in great abundance.

And the people that were therein he brought forth and he put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and he made them pass through the brick kiln; and so he did to all the cities of the children of Amon. And Dovid and all the people returned to Yerushalayim.
And it came to pass after this, that Avshalom the son of Dovid had a fair sister whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of Dovid loved her.
And Amnon was distressed to the point of making himself sick, on account of Tamar his sister, for she was a virgin; and it seemed difficult in Amnon's eyes to do anything unto her.
And Amnon had a friend, whose name was Yonadav the son of Shimah the brother of Dovid; and Yonadav was a very sly man.
And he said to him, "Why are you becoming so thin, O' son of the king, from morning to morning? Will you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him, "I love Tamar, the sister of Avshalom."

And Yonadav said to him: "Lie down on your bed and feign sickness, and when your father comes to see you, say to him: "Let my sister Tamar come now, and let her give me bread to eat, and prepare the food before my eyes, that I may see and eat from her hand."
And Amnon lay down and feigned sickness; and the king came to see him, and Amnon said to the king, "Let my sister Tamar come now, and make two dumplings before my eyes; that I may eat from her hand."
And Dovid sent home to Tamar saying, "Go now to your brother Amnon's house, and prepare the food for him."
And Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house, and he was lying down. And she took the dough, and kneaded it, and she prepared the dumplings before his eyes, and she cooked the dumplings.
And she took the pan and poured before him: but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, "Take everyone out from me." And everyone went out from him.
And Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the chamber that I may eat from your hand." And Tamar took the dumplings that she had made and brought them to Amnon her brother into the chamber.
And she brought them near to him to eat, and he took hold of her and said to her, "Come lie with me, my sister."
And she said to him, "No, my brother, do not force me, for it is not done so in Yisroel; do not do this wanton deed.
And I, where shall I lead my shame? And you, you shall be like one of the profligate men in Yisroel. And now I beg of you to speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you."
But he would not heed her and he overpowered her, and forced her, and lay with her.
And Amnon hated her with very great hatred, for greater was the hatred with which he hated her than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, "Get up go."
And she said to him, "Do not do this wrong greater than the other one that you did to me, by sending me away." But he would not listen to her.
And he called his youth, his servant, and he said, "Send now this one away from me, outside, and lock the door after her!
Now she had on a striped tunic, for in this manner the king's virgin daughters dressed, in robes. And his servant brought her outside, and locked the door after her.
And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of many colours that was on her; and she laid her hand on her head, and went her way, crying aloud as she went.

And Avshalom her brother said to her: "Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now, my sister, remain silent; he is your brother; do not take this thing to heart!" And Tamar stayed in solitude in her brother Avshalom's house.
And King Dovid heard all these things and became very angry.
And Avshalom spoke with Amnon neither bad nor good, for Avshalom hated Amnon because he had forced his sister, Tamar.
And it happened after two whole years, that Avshalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which is beside Efraim; and Avshalom invited all the king's sons.
And Avshalom came to the King, and said, "Behold now, your servant has sheepshearers, let the King and his servants please go with your servant."
And the King said to Avshalom, "No my son, let us not all go, lest we impose on you." And he pressed him, but he would not go, but he did bless him.
And Avshalom said, "If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us." And the King said to him, "Why should he go with you?"
But Avshalom pressed him, and he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.

And Avshalom commanded his youths saying, "Please take note, when Amnon's heart is merry with wine, and when I say to you, 'Smite Amnon,' then kill him, fear not; have I not commanded you to be courageous and valiant?"
And Avshalom's servants did to Amnon as Avshalom had commanded. And all the king's sons arose, and they rode off, each one on his mule, and they fled.
And it came to pass, while they were on their way, that the news came to Dovid, saying: "Avshalom has slain all the king's sons, and not one of them is left."
And the king arose, and tore his clothes, and lay on the ground, and all his servants stood with their clothes torn.

And Yonadav, the son of Dovid's brother Shimah, answered and said, "Let not my master say that they have killed all the young men, the king's sons; for Amnon alone is dead; for by the mouth of Avshalom this had been arranged from the day he forced Tamar his sister.
And now, let not my master the king put to his heart the thing to say that all the king's sons are dead; but only Amnon is dead."
And Avshalom fled. And the young man that kept watch raised his eyes and looked, and behold a large crowd was coming from the way behind him, by the hillside.
And Yonadav said to the king, "Behold the king's sons have come, as your servant said, so it was."
And it was as soon as he had finished speaking that, behold, the king's sons came and raised up their voices and cried, and also the king and all his servants wept profusely.
And Avshalom fled and he went to Talmai, the son of Amichud, the king of Geshur. And he mourned for his son all the days.
And Avshalom fled, and he went to Geshur, and he was there three years.
And King Dovid longed to go forth to Avshalom; for he was comforted concerning Amnon, being that he was dead.
And Yoav the son of Tzeruyah knew that the king's heart for Avshalom.

And Yoav sent to Teko'a and took from there a wise woman; and he said to her: "Please pretend to be a mourner, and please put on mourning clothes, and do not anoint yourself with oil, but be as a woman who has mourned many days for the dead.
And come to the king and speak to him in this manner." And Yoav put the words into her mouth.
And the woman of Teko'a spoke to the king, and fell to the ground, and prostrated herself; and she said: 'Save, O' king'.
And the king said to her: 'What ails you?' And she said: 'Truly I am a woman a widow, and my husband is dead.
And your handmaid had two sons, and they both fought in the field, and there was no rescuer between them, and one struck the other and killed him.

And, behold, the whole family rose against your handmaid, and said: "Deliver the one that struck his brother whom he slew, and so destroy also the heir; and so they shall quench my coal which is left, so as not to leave my husband a name or a remainder upon the face of the earth."
And the king said to the woman, "Go to your house, and I will give orders about you."
And the woman of Teko'a said to the king, "On me, my master, the king, be the iniquity, and on my father's house; and the king and his throne be guiltless."
And the king said, "Who ever speaks to you, bring him to me, and he shall no longer continue to touch you."

And she said, "I beg you, let the king remember Havayah your Elokim that the avenger of blood destroy not excessively so that they destroy not my son." And he said, "As Havayah lives, if one hair of your son shall fall to the earth."
And the woman said, "May your handmaid speak a word with my master the king?" And he said, "Speak."

And the woman said, "Why have you thought such a thing about the people of Elokim? that the king in speaking this word has done so accidentally, so that the king shall not bring back his banished one.
For die we must, and as water that is spilt on the ground which cannot be gathered up again; and Elokim favors not a soul, but He devises means that he that is banished be not cast from Him.

And now my motive for having come to speak of this thing to the king my master because the people have made me afraid; and your maidservant said: I will now speak to the king, perhaps the king will perform the request of his handmaid.
For the king will hear, to deliver his maidservant from the hand of the man destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of Elokim.

And your handmaid said, 'Let, I pray, the word of my master the king be for comfort, for as an angel of Elokim so is my master the king, to discern the good and the bad; and Havayah your Elokim may be with you'."
And the king answered and he said to the woman, "I beg you not to hide from me anything that I shall ask you." And the woman said: "Let my master the king please speak."

And the king said: "Is the hand of Yoav with you in all this?" And the woman answered and said, "As your soul lives, my master the king, if anyone can turn to the right or to the left from all that my master the king has spoken, for your servant Yoav he bade me, and he put in the mouth of your handmaid all these words.
In order to bring about the face of the matter, has your servant Yoav done this thing; and my master is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of Elokim to know all that is in the earth."
And the king said to Yoav: "Behold now, you have done this thing, now go bring back the young man Avshalom."

And Yoav fell on his face to the ground and he prostrated himself, and he blessed the king; and Yoav said: "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, my master, O' king, in that the king has done the request of your servant."
And Yoav arose and went to Geshur, and he brought Avshalom to Yerushalayim.
And the king said: "Let him turn to his house, but my face let him not see." And Avshalom turned to his house, and the king's face he saw not.
Now like Avshalom there was not a man in all Yisroel as beautiful, to be as praiseworthy; from the sole of his feet to the crown of his head, there was no blemish in him.

And when he shaved his head-and it was at every year's end that he shaved it; because the hair was heavy on him, then he would shave it- he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels, after the king's weight.
And to Avshalom were born three sons and one daughter whose name was Tamar; and she was a woman of beautiful appearance.
And Avshalom dwelt in Yerushalayim two full years; and the king's face he did not see.
And Avshalom sent to Yoav, to send him to the king; and he would not come to him: and he sent again a second time, and he would not come.
And he said to his servants, "See, Yoav's field is near mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire." And Avshalom's servants set the field on fire.
And Yoav arose, and he came to Avshalom to his house, and he said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"

And Avshalom said to Yoav, "Behold, I have sent to you, saying: 'Come here,' that I may send you to the king to say: 'Why have I come from Geshur?' it would be better for me were I still there; and now I will see the king's face; and if there be iniquity in me, let him kill me."

And Yoav came to the king, and he told him: and he called for Avshalom, and he came to the king, and he prostrated himself to him on his face to the ground before the king; and the king kissed Avshalom.
And it came to pass after this, that Avshalom made for himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men were running before him.

And Avshalom would rise up, and stand beside the path of the gate; and it was any man that would have a suit to come to the king for judgment, then Avshalom called him and he said: "From what city are you?" and he said: "Of one of the tribes of Yisroel is your servant.
And Avshalom said to him: "See your words are good and right; but there is none of the king's to hear you."
And Avshalom said, "Oh, who will appoint me judge in the land, and every man who has a quarrel or suit, will come to me, then I will do him justice."
And it would be, when a man came near to prostrate himself before him, that he put forth his hand and took hold of him, and kissed him.
And Avshalom did likewise to all the Bnei Yisroel that came to the king for judgment. And Avshalom stole the hearts of the men of Yisroel.
And it came to pass at the end of forty years; and Avshalom said to the king; "Allow me to go, I beg you, and pay my vow which I have vowed to Havayah in Chevron.
For your servant vowed a vow during my stay in Geshur in Aram, saying: 'If Havayah shall bring me back to Yerushalayim, then I will serve Havayah'."
And the king said to him: "Go in peace." And he arose and went to Chevron.
And Avshalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Yisroel saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the shofar, then you shall say: 'Avshalom is king in Chevron'."
And with Avshalom went two hundred men invited; and went in their innocence; and did not know of anything.

And Avshalom sent for Achitofel the Giloni, Dovid's counsellor, from his city, from Giloh, as he offered the sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong, and the people with Avshalom were steadily increasing.
And the messenger came to Dovid saying, "The hearts of the people of Yisroel are after Avshalom."

And Dovid said to all his servants that were with him in Yerushalayim: "Arise and let us flee, for there will be no escape for us from Avshalom. Go quickly lest he hurry and overtake us, and bring upon us evil, and smite the city with the edge of the sword."
And the king's servants said to the king, "Whatever my master the king shall choose, behold your servants."
And the king went forth, and all his household were right behind him. And the king led the ten women concubines to keep the house.
And the king went forth, and all the people were right behind him: and they remained standing at the farthest house.
And all his servants passed on beside him, and all the archers and all the slingers, and all the Gittim, six hundred men that came after him from Gat, passed on before the king.
And the king said to Ittai the Gitti; 'Why do you also go with us? return, and abide with the king; for you are a foreigner, and if you are wont to wander, your own place.
yesterday you came, and today I should move you about with us, seeing that I go wherever I can go? Return and take back your brothers with you, kindness and truth."

And Ittai answered the king and said, 'As Havayah lives, and as my master the king lives, that in the place where my master the king shall be, whether for life or for death, for there shall your servant be.'
And Dovid said to Ittai, "Go and pass over." And Ittai the Gitti passed over and all his men and all the little ones that were with him.
And all the land wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over; and the king passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over toward the way of the wilderness.

And lo, Tzadok also, and all the Leviim with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of Elokim: and they set down the ark of Elokim, and Evyatar went up, until all the people had finished passing out of the city.
And the king said to Tzadok, "Carry back the ark of Elokim to the city; if I find favor in the eyes of Havayah, then He will bring me back, and He will show me it, and His habitation.
But if so says, 'I do not want you,' behold, here I am, let Him do to me as seems good in His eyes."
And the king said to Tzadok the priest: 'Do you see? return to the city in peace, and Achima'atz your son, and Yehonatan the son of Evyatar, your two sons, with you.
See, I will tarry in the plains of the wilderness, until there comes word from you to announce to me.'
And Tzadok and Evyatar returned the ark of Elokim to Yerushalayim, and they abode there.

And Dovid went up by the ascent of the olives, weeping as he went up. And he had his head covered and he went barefoot; and all the people that were with him every man covered his head, weeping as they went up.
And told Dovid saying, "Achitofel is among the conspirators with Avshalom." And Dovid said, "Make foolish, I beg you, the counsel of Achitofel, O' Havayah."
And Dovid was coming to the top where he would prostrate himself to Elokim, and behold, towards him Chushai the Arki with his shirt torn, and earth upon his head.
And Dovid said to him, "If you pass on with me you will be a burden to me.

But if you return to the city and you say to Avshalom, 'I O' king will be your servant, just as I was previously your father's servant,' and now I am your servant; then you will to frustrate for me the counsel of Achitofel.
And have you not there with you Tzadok and Evyatar the priest? And it shall be that everything you hear from the king's house, you shall tell to Tzadok and Evyatar the priests.
And, behold, they have there with them their two sons, Achima'atz to Tzadok, and Yehonatan to Evyatar, and through them you shall send to me everything you hear."
And Chushai the Arki, the friend of Dovid, came into the city, and Avshalom coming to Yerushalayim.

And Dovid was a little past the top, and behold, Tziva the servant of Mefiboshet toward him, with a pair of saddled asses, and upon them two hundred of bread, and a hundred clusters of raisins, and a hundred summer fruit, and a flask of wine.

And the king said to Tziva, "What for are these to you?" And Tziva said, 'the asses are for the king's household to ride on; and the bread and the summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine for the faint to drink in the wilderness'.
And the king said, "And where is your master's son?" And Tziva said to the king, "Behold he lives in Yerushalayim, for he said, "Today the house of Yisroel will restore my father's kingdom to me."
And the king said to Tziva, "Behold, all that belongs to Mefiboshet is yours." And Tziva said, "I prostrate myself; let me find favor in your eyes, my master O' king."
And king Dovid came to Bachurim and, behold, there came out of there a man from the family of the house of Shaul, whose name was Shimi, the son of Gera, coming forth and cursing.
And he threw stones at Dovid, and at all king Dovid's servants and at all the people and at all the mighty men who were on his right and on his left hand.
And so Shimi said in his curse, "Begone, begone, you man of blood, and you wicked man.

Havayah has returned upon you all the blood of the house of Shaul, in whose stead you have reigned; and Havayah has given the kingdom into the hands of Avshalom your son; and behold you are in your own evil for you are a man of blood."
And Avishai the son of Tzeruyah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my master the king? Let me go over, I beg you, and remove his head."
And the king said, "What is it between me and you, sons of Tzeruyah? So let him curse, because Havayah has said to him, 'Curse Dovid'; who then shall say, 'Why have you done so'?"
And Dovid said to Avishai and to all his servants, "Behold my son who came from my body seeks my life; how much more now the Binyamini? Let him alone, and let him curse; for Havayah has bidden him.
Perhaps Havayah will see my eye, and Havayah will return to me good instead of his curse on this day."
And Dovid and his men went by the road; and Shimi went along the hillside opposite him, going and cursing and he threw stones toward him, and he threw earth.
And the king, and all the people that were with him were weary, and he refreshed himself there.
And Avshalom, and all the people, the men of Yisroel, came to Yerushalayim; and Achitofel with him.
And it came to pass when Chushai the Arki, Dovid's friend, had come to Avshalom, that Chushai said to Avshalom, " live the king, live the king."
And Avshalom said to Chushai, "Is this your kindness to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"
And Chushai said to Avshalom, "No, but to whom Havayah and these people, and all the men of Yisroel have chosen, to him will I be, and with him will I abide.
Secondly, whom should I serve? not in the presence of his son? As I have served in your father's presence, so will I be in your presence."
And Avshalom said to Achitofel, "Give yourself counsel what we shall do."

And Achitofel said to Avshalom, "Come in to your father's concubines that he has left to keep the house; and all Yisroel will hear that you are abhorred of your father; then the hands of all that are with you will be strengthened."
And they spread for Avshalom a tent upon the roof; and Avshalom came to his father's concubines before the eyes of all Yisroel.
And the counsel of Achitofel, which he counselled in those days was as if a man inquired of the word of Elokim: so was all the counsel of Achitofel both to Dovid and to Avshalom.
And Achitofel said to Avshalom: "Let me now choose twelve thousand men, and I will rise and pursue Dovid tonight.
And I will come upon him while he is weary and weak-handed, and I will startle him: and all the people that are with him will flee, and I will smite the king alone.
And I will bring back all the people to you; when all shall have returned, the man whom you seek then all the people will be at peace."
And the thing seemed right to the eyes of Avshalom, and to all the elders of Yisroel.
And Avshalom said, "Now call Chushai the Arki also, and let us hear what he too has to say."
And Chushai came to Avshalom; and Avshalom spoke to him saying, "In this manner has Achitofel spoken; shall we do his bidding? If not, then you speak."
And Chushai said to Avshalom, "The counsel which Achitofel has counseled this time is not good."

And Chushai saying, "You know your father and his men that they are mighty men, and they are of embittered spirit, as a bear in the field, bereft of cubs, and your father is a man of war, and he will not lodge with the people.

Behold, now he is hidden in one of the pits or one of the places; and it will come to pass, if there fall among them at the first, then someone will hear it and say, 'There has been a massacre among the people that are behind Avshalom.'
And even if he be valiant whose heart is as the heart of a lion will utterly melt; for all Yisroel knows that your father is a mighty man, and valiant men are they that are with him.
Therefore I counsel, that all Yisroel be gathered together to you, from Dan to Be'er Sheva as many as the sand that is by the sea; and you personally go to battle.

And we shall come upon him in some place where he is found, and we shall light upon him, as the dew falls on the ground; and there shall not be left of him, and of all the men that are with him, even one.
And if he withdraws himself into a city, then all of Yisroel shall bring up ropes to that city and we will drag it to the valley until there shall not be found there even one small stone."

And Avshalom and all the men of Yisroel said, "the counsel of Chushai the Arki is better than the counsel of Achitofel,"-for Havayah had ordained to frustrate the good counsel of Achitofel in order that Havayah might bring evil upon Avshalom.
And Chushai said to Tzadok and Evyatar the priests, "In thus and thus manner did Achitofel counsel Avshalom and the elders of Yisroel; and thus and thus have I counseled.
And now, send quickly, and tell Dovid saying: "Do not lodge the night in the plains of the wilderness, but pass over, lest the king be destroyed, and all the people that are with him."
And Yehonatan and Achima'atz were standing by Ein-Rogel; and the maidservant went and she told them that they should go notify King Dovid; for they were not to be seen coming into the city.
But a lad spotted them, and told Avshalom; and they both went speedily away to the house of a man in Bachurim, and he had a well in his courtyard; and they lowered themselves there.
And the woman took and spread the covering over the mouth of the well and she spread groats upon it, and nothing was known.

And Avshalom's servants came to the woman in the house, and they said, "Where are Achima'atz and Yehonatan?" And the woman said to them, "They have forded the river." And they sought but could not find; and they returned to Yerushalayim.

And it came to pass after their departure, that they came up out of the well, and they went and they told King Dovid, "Arise and cross the water quickly, for thus has Achitofel counseled against you."
And Dovid arose, and all the people that were with him, and they crossed the Yarden. By the morning light not one of them was missing that had not crossed the Yarden.

And Achitofel saw that his counsel was not done, and he saddled his ass, and he arose, and he went to his house, to his city, and he gave charge to his household and he strangled himself, and he died, and was buried in the sephulcre of his father.
And Dovid had come to Machanayim, and Avshalom passed over the Yarden, he and all the men of Yisroel with him.

And Amasa, had Avshalom set in place of Yoav over the host; and Amasa was the son of a man, whose name was Yitra the Yisroeli, who came to Avigayil the daughter of Nachash the sister of Tzeruyah, Yoav's mother.
And Yisroel and Avshalom encamped in the land of Gilad.
And it came to pass, when Dovid came to Machanayim, that Shovi the son of Nachash from Rabbah of the children of Amon and Machir the son of Amiel of Lo-Devar, and Barzilai the Giladi of Rogelim.
Beds and bowls, and earthen vessels, and wheat and barley and flour and parched grain; and beans, and lentils and parched grain.

And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine they presented to Dovid and to the people that were with him, to eat, for they said, "The people are hungry, faint, and thirsty from the wilderness."
And Dovid numbered the people that were with him, and he placed over them captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds.

And Dovid sent forth the people, a third in the hands of Yoav, a third in the hands of Avishai the son of Tzeruyah, Yoav's brother, and a third under the hands of Ittai the Gitti. And the king said to the people, "I, too, will go forth with you."

And the people said, "You shall not go forth; for if we flee they will not pay attention to us; even if half of us should die, they will not pay attention to us, for now you are ten thousand of us; and therefore now it is better that you be for us from the city as aid."
And the king said to them: "What seems best to you, I will do." And the king stood by the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.
And the king commanded Yoav and Avishai and Ittai saying: "Deal gently for me with the youth, with Avshalom." And all the people heard when the king commanded all the captains regarding Avshalom.
And the people went out into the field against Yisroel; and the battle took place in the forest of Efraim.
And the people of Yisroel were beaten there before the servants of Dovid, and the slaughter there, on that day, was very great, twenty thousand men.
And the battle spread from there over the face of all the land; and the forest devoured more of the people, than the sword devoured on that day.

And Avshalom chanced to come before the servants of Dovid. And Avshalom was riding upon his mule, and the mule came under the thick boughs of the great terebinth, and his head caught hold in the terebinth, and he was placed between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was beneath him passed on.
And a man saw it and told Yoav. And he said, "Behold I saw Avshalom hanging in a terebinth."
And Yoav said to the man who told him, "Now if you had seen it, then why did you not smite him there to the ground? And it would have been upon me to give you ten silver, and a belt."

And the man said to Yoav: "Though I should weigh on my palms a thousand of silver, I would not stretch out my hand against the king's son, because before our ears did the king charge you and Avishai and Ittai saying, 'Take care whoever of the youth, of Avshalom.'
Even if I would deal falsely with myself, now nothing can be hidden from the king, and you would stand from afar."
And Yoav said, "I shall no longer request of you." And he took three darts in his hand and thrust them into Avshalom's heart while he was yet alive in the heart of the terebinth.
And there circled about ten young men who were Yoav's armor bearers, and they struck Avshalom, and killed him.
And Yoav blew with a shofar, and the people returned from pursuing after Yisroel; for Yoav held back the people.
And they took Avshalom, and they cast him in the forest, into the great pit, and they placed over him a very large heap of stones; and all of Yisroel fled each to his tents.

And Avshalom had taken and established for himself in his lifetime, the monument which is in the king's valley for he said, "I have no son in order to cause to remember my name;" and he called the monument after his own name, and they called it Yad Avshalom until this day.
And Achima'atz, the son of Tzadok said, "Let me now run and bring news to the king that Havayah has avenged him from the hand of his enemies."
And Yoav said to him: "You are not the man to bring news this day, but you shall bring news another day, but this day you shall not bring news, because the king's son is dead."
And Yoav said to the Kushi "Go tell the king what you have seen." And the Kushi bowed down to Yoav, and ran.

And Achima'atz the son of Tzadok continued again, and said to Yoav, "Come what may, please allow me to run after the Kushi." And Yoav said, "Why should you to run, my son, since for you there is no given for the news!"
"But, come what may,", "I will run." And he said to him, "Run" And Achima'atz ran by the way of the plain, and he went ahead of the Kushi.
And Dovid sat between the two gates; and the watchman went up to the roof of the gate to the wall, and he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold a man running alone.
And the watchman called out, and told the king. And the king said, "If he is alone, he has news to tell." And he came nearer and nearer.
And the watchman saw another man running; and the watchman called the gatekeepers, and he said, "Behold, there is a man running alone." And the king said, "This one also brings news."
And the watchman said, "I see the running of the first one is like the running of Achima'atz the son of Tzadok." And the king said, "This is a good man, and he comes with good news."

And Achima'atz called, and said to the king, "Peace" And he bowed down to the king on his face, to the ground, and said, "Blessed is Havayah your Elokim who has delivered up the men that raised up their hand against my master the king."
And the king said, " peace with the young man Avshalom?" And Achima'atz answered, "I saw a great crowd when Yoav sent the servant of the king and your servant, but I did not know what it was."
And the king said, "Turn aside and stand there." And he turned aside and stood.
And, behold, the Kushi came; and the Kushi said, "Let my master the king receive the tidings that Havayah has avenged you today from all that rose up against you."

And the king said to the Kushi, "Is all well with the young man Avshalom?" And the Kushi said, "Let the enemies of my master the king be like that young man, and so with all those that have risen against you for evil."

And the king trembled, and he went up to the upper chamber of the gate, and wept; and thus he said, as he went, "O' my son Avshalom, my son, my son Avshalom! Would I have died in your stead, O' Avshalom my son, my son!"
And it was told to Yoav, "Behold the king is weeping and mourning over Avshalom."
And the victory that day into mourning for all the people; for the people heard on that day, saying: "The king is saddened over his son."
And the people sneaked that day into the city, as people that are ashamed sneak away when they flee in battle.
And the king covered his face, and the king cried with loud voice: 'O' my son Avshalom, O' Avshalom, my son, my son!"

And Yoav came to the king, into the house; and he said, "Today you have embarrassed all your servants, who have today saved your life, the lives of your sons and daughters, the lives of your wives, and the lives of your concubines.

By loving those that hate you, and hating those that love you; for on this day you have declared that you regard neither princes nor servants, since I perceive today that if Avshalom had lived and we all had died today, then it would have been proper in your eyes.

And now arise, go out, and speak to the heart of your servants, for I swear by Havayah, that you do not go forth, not one man will remain with you tonight. Now this will be worse for you than all the misfortune that has befallen you from your youth until now."

And the king arose, and sat in the gate. And all the people were notified saying, "Behold the king is sitting in the gate." And all the people came before the king, but Yisroel fled every man to his tents.

And all the people argued with one another throughout all of Yisroel by saying: 'The king delivered us out of the hand of our enemies, and he saved us out of the hands of the Pelishtim; and now he flee out of the land from before Avshalom.
And Avshalom whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now, therefore, why do you remain silent about returning the king?"

And King Dovid sent to Tzadok and to Evyatar the priests, saying, "Speak to the elders of Yehudah, saying, 'Why should you be the last to return the king to his house? ' -while the talk of all Yisroel has come to the king to his house?
You are my brethren; you are my own bone and flesh; why then should you be the last to return the king?
And to Amasa you shall say, 'Are you not my bone and my flesh? So shall Elokim do to me, and even more, if you shall not be captain of the host before me continually in Yoav's stead'."
And he swayed the heart of all the men of Yehudah, as one man; And they sent to the king, "Return you, with all your servants."
And the king returned, and he came to the Yarden. And Yehudah came to Gilgal to go towards the king and to lead the king across the Yarden.
And Shimi the son of Gera, the Binyamini who was from Bachurim hurried and came down with the men of Yehudah to meet King Dovid.
And a thousand men of Binyamin were with him, and Tziva the servant of the house of Shaul, and his fifteen sons and twenty servants with him, and they split the Yarden before the king.
And the barge crossed over to bring the king's household across, and to do what would be pleasing in his eyes. And Shimi the son of Gera fell down before the king when he was crossing the Yarden.

And he said to the king, "Let not my master impute iniquity to me, nor remember that which your servant sinned on the day that my master the king went out of Yerushalayim, that the king should take it to his heart.
For your servant knows that I have sinned and I have therefore come this day the first of all the House of Yosef to go down towards my master the king."
And Avishai the son of Tzeruyah responded and said, "In exchange for this shall Shimi not be put to death for having cursed Havayah's anointed?"

And Dovid said, "What is it between me and you, sons of Tzeruyah, that you should become a hindrance to me today? Shall any man be put to death today in Yisroel? For do I not know that today I am king over Yisroel?"
And the king said to Shimi, "You shall not die." And the king swore to him.

And Mefiboshet the son of Shaul came down towards the king; and he had not washed his feet, nor did he trim his mustache, and his clothes he did not wash, from the day of the king's departure until the day that he came in peace.
