And it came to pass, when he came to Yerushalayim towards the king, that the king said to him, "Why had you not gone with me, Mefiboshet?"
And he said, "My master the king, my servant deceived me; for your servant said, "I will saddle me an ass so that I may ride on it and accompany the king," since your servant is lame.
And he slandered your servant to my master the king; but my master the king is as an angel of Elokim: do therefore what is good in your eyes.

For all of my father's house were nothing more than deserving of death of my master the king; yet you placed your servant among them that eat at your table. What more right have I to appeal further to the king?"
And the king said to him, "Why do you speak further concerning this matter? I say; You and Tziva divide the land."
And Mefiboshet said to the king, "Let him take all, now that my master the king has arrived safely to his house."
And Barzilai the Giladi came down from Rogelim; and he crossed the Yarden with the king, to escort him across the Yarden.
Now Barzilai was a very old man, eighty years old, and he had sustained the king when he stayed at Machanayim, for he was a very great man.
And the king said to Barzilai, "You come over with me, and I will sustain you with me in Yerushalayim."
And Barzilai said to the king, "How many are the days of my life that I should go up with the king to Yerushalayim?

I am eighty years old this day, can I discern between good and bad? Or can your servant taste what I eat and drink? Or can I still listen to the voice of singers and songstresses? Why then, should your servant be yet a burden to my master the king?"
A short way shall your servant go past the Yarden with the king; but why should the king recompense me with such reward?

Allow your servant, please, to turn back, so that I may die in my own city by the grave of my father and mother. Here, however, is your servant Kimham, let him go over with my master the king and do to him what is good in your eyes."
And the king said, "Kimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him what seems good in your eyes. Now, anything that you shall request of me I shall do for you."
And all the people went over the Yarden and the king went over; and the king kissed Barzilai and he blessed him: and he returned to his place.
And the king went over to Gilgal, and Kimham went over with him: and all the people of Yehudah brought the king over, and also half the people of Yisroel.

And, behold, all the men of Yisroel came to the king, and they said to the king, "Why did our brothers the men of Yehudah, steal you away; by having brought the king and his household over the Yarden, and all of Dovid's men with him?"
And all the men of Yehudah answered the men of Yisroel, "Because the king is near to me; why are you so angered over this matter? Have we eaten of the king or has any present been gifted us?"

And the men of Yisroel answered the man of Yehudah and he said, "I have ten parts in the king and am therefore to Dovid than to you. Why then did you slight me? Now was not my word the very first to return my king?" And the words of the men of Yehudah were harsher than the words of the men of Yisroel.

Now there chanced to be there a base man, whose name was Sheva, the son of Bichri, a Binyamini; and he blew a 'shofar' and declared, "We have no portion of Dovid, neither have we an inheritence in the son of Yishai; every man to his tents, O' Yisroel."
And all the men of Yisroel went up from after Dovid, following Sheva the son of Bichri, but the men of Yehudah cleaved to their king from the Yarden until Yerushalayim.

And Dovid came to his house in Yerushalayim, and the king took the ten women concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and he put them in a guard-house where he sustained them, but he came not upon them. And they remained bound as widows alive until the day of their death.
And the king said to Amasa, "Call together for me the men of Yehudah three days, then be here present."
And Amasa went to call together the men of Yehudah, but he tarried past the set time which he had appointed him.

And Dovid said to Avishai, "Now Sheva the son of Bichri will cause us more harm than did Avshalom; take you your master's servants and pursue after him, lest he find for himself fortified cities and save our eyes."
And Yoav's men went after him with the archers and the slingers and all the warriors; and they went out of Yerushalayim to pursue Sheva the son of Bichri.

They were by the great stone which is in Givon, when Amasa came before them. And Yoav was girded with his military coat as apparel, and thereon was a girded sword in its sheath fastened to his loins and he went forth, and it fell out.
And Yoav said to Amasa, "Is all well with you, my brother?" And Yoav's right hand took hold of Amasa's beard to kiss him.

And Amasa took no heed of the sword that was in Yoav's hand; and he struck him with it to the fifth rib and he spilled out his bowels to the ground, and though he did not repeat, he died. And Yoav and Avishai his brother pursued Sheva the son of Bichri.
And one of Yoav's young men stood by him and he said, "He that favors Yoav, and he that is for Dovid, let him follow Yoav."

And Amasa was wallowing in blood in the middle of the highway. And the man saw that all the people remained standing, so he veered Amasa off the highway into the field, and he threw a garment over him when he saw that everyone who came upon him stood still.
When he was removed from the highway, all the people passed on after Yoav to pursue Sheva the son of Bichri.
And he passed through all the tribes of Yisroel to Hevel, and to Beit Ma'achah, and all the Berim; and they gathered together and they went after him too.

And they came and they besieged him in Hevel of Beit-maacah, and they spilled a mound against the city and it stood with its inner wall; and all the people that were with Yoav were battering to throw down the wall.
And a wise woman called out from within the city, 'Hear, hear; say, I pray you, to Yoav: 'Come closer to here so that I may speak to you.'
And he came near to her, and the woman said, "Are you Yoav?" And he said, "I am" And she said to him: 'Hear the words of your handmaid.' And he said: 'I am listening.'
And she spoke saying: "Surely they should have spoken first to say, had they inquired of Hevel, and so would they have made peace.
I am of that are peaceful and faithful to Yisroel; do you seek to destroy a city and a mother in Yisroel? Why should you swallow up the inheritance of Havayah?"
And Yoav answered: 'Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up, or that I should destroy.

The matter is not so; but a man of the hills of Efraim named Sheva the son of Bichri has lifted his hand against the king, against Dovid; Give us him alone and I will depart from the city.' And the woman said to Yoav, "His head shall be thrown to you over the wall."

And the woman came to all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheva the son of Bichri and threw it to Yoav. And he blew the shofar, and they dispersed from the city, every man to his tents. And Yoav returned to Yerushalayim to the king.
And Yoav was over the entire army of Yisroel; and Benayahu the son of Yehoyada was over the archers and the slingers.
And Adoram was over the tribute; and Yehoshafat the son of Achilud was recorder.
And Shvah was scribe; and Tzadok and Evyatar were the priests.
And Ira the Ya'iri was a chief official to Dovid.

And there was a famine in the days of Dovid for three years, year after year. And Dovid sought the face of Havayah. And Havayah said: " for Shaul, and for his bloody house, because he put to death the Givonim."

And the king called the Givonim and said to them-now the Givonim were not of the children of Yisroel, but of the remnant of the Emorim; and the children of Yisroel had sworn to them; but Shaul sought to slay them in his zeal for the sake of the children of Yisroel and Yehudah.
And Dovid said to the Givonim, "What shall I do for you? And with what shall I make atonement so that you shall bless the inheritance of Havayah?"
And the Givonim said to him, "We have no of silver and gold with Shaul, or with his house, and we to put to death any man in Yisroel." And he said, "What do you request I shall do for you?"
And they said to the king, "The man who consumed us and who plotted us that we be destroyed from remaining within any of Yisroel's borders.
Let there be delivered to us seven men from among his sons, and we will hang them for Havayah in Givat Shaul, the chosen of Havayah." And the king said, "I shall deliver."
But the king took pity on Mefiboshet, the son of Yehonatan the son of Shaul, because of Havayah's oath that was between Dovid and Yehonatan the son of Shaul.

And the king took the two sons of Ritzpah the daughter of Ayah, whom she bore to Shaul, Armoni and Mefiboshet; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Shaul, whom she bore to Adriel the son of Barzilai the Mecholati.

And he delivered them into the hands of the Givonim, and they hanged them in the mountain before Havayah, and they fell all seven together. And they were put to death in the days of the harvest, in the first, at the beginning of the barley harvest.

And Ritzpah the daughter of Ayah took the sackcloth and she spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of the harvest until water was poured upon them from heaven; and she allowed not the birds of the heaven to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
And it was told to Dovid what Ritzpah the daughter of Ayah, the concubine of Shaul, had done.

And Dovid went and he took the bones of Shaul and the bones of Yehonatan his son from the men of Yavesh- gilead, who had stolen them from the street of Beit-She'an, where the Pelishtim had hanged them, on the day that the Pelishtim slew Shaul in Gilboa.
And he brought up from there the bones of Shaul and the bones of Yehonatan his son; and they gathered the bones of those that were hanged.

And they buried the bones of Shaul and Yehonatan his son in the country of Binyamin in Tzela, in the sephulcre of Kish his father; and they did all that the king commanded. And Elokim was entreated for the land after that.
And the Pelishtim waged war again with Yisroel; and Dovid went down with his servants and they fought against the Pelishtim, but Dovid became faint.
And Yishbi, who was one of the sons of Refa'ah was in Nov; and the weight of his spear was three hundred of brass in weight; and he was girded with new armor, and he thought to smite Dovid.

But Avishai the son of Tzeruyah aided him, and he struck the Pelishti, and killed him. Then the men of Dovid swore to him saying, "You shall no longer go out with us to battle, so that you extinguish not the lamp of Yisroel."
And it came to pass after this, that there was war again at Gob with the Pelishtim; Then Sibchai the Chushati slew Saf, who was one of the sons of Refa'ah.
And there was war again Gob with the Pelishtim; and Elhanan the son of Ya'arei-oregim the Beit-lehemite slew Golyat the Gitti, and the staff of his spear was as the weavers' beam.
And there was again war at Gat, and there was a man of great stature, and the fingers of his hands and the toes of his feet were six and six, totalling twenty four; and he too was born to Orpah.
And he taunted Yisroel, and Yehonatan the son of Shimea, Dovid's brother, smote him.
These four were born to Refa'ah in Gat; and they fell by the hand of Dovid, and by the hand of his servants.
And Dovid spoke to Havayah the words of this song, on the day that Havayah delivered him from the hand of all his enemies, and from the hand of Shaul;
And he said, "Havayah is my rock and my fortress, and a rescuer to me.
Elokim is my rock, under whom I take cover; My shield, and the horn of my salvation, my support, and my refuge; my savior Who saves me from violence.
With praise, I call out to Havayah, for from my enemies I shall be saved.
For the pains of death have encompassed me; streams of scoundrels would affright me.
Bands of the nether world have surrounded me; the snares of death confronted me.
When I am in distress, I call upon Havayah, yes I call upon my Elokim: and out of His abode He hears my voice, and my cry enters His ears.
Then the earth shook and quaked, the foundations of heaven did tremble; and they were shaken when He was angered.
Smoke went up in His nostrils, and fire out of His mouth did devour; coals flamed forth from Him.
And He bent the heavens and He came down; and thick darkness was under His feet.
And He rode upon a cherub and did fly; He was seen upon the wings of the wind.
And He fixed darkness about Him as booths; gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.
From the brightness before Him flamed forth coals of fire.
Havayah thundered from heaven; and the Most High gave forth His voice.
And He sent out arrows and He scattered them, lightning and He discomfited them.
And the depths of the sea appeared; the foundations of the world were laid bare, by the rebuke of Havayah and the blast of the breath of His nostrils.
He sent from on high He took me; He drew me out of many waters.
He delivered me from my mighty enemy; from them that hated me; for they were too powerful for me.
They confronted me on the day of my calamity; but Havayah was a support to me.
And He brought me forth into a wide place; He delivered me because He took delight in me.
Havayah rewarded me according to my righteousness; According to the cleanness of my hands He recompensed me.
For I have kept the ways of Havayah and have not wickedly departed from my Elokim.
For all His ordinances were before me; and His statutes, I did not depart from it.
And I was single-hearted toward Him, and I kept myself from my iniquity.
And Havayah has recompensed me according to my righteousness; according to my cleanness before His eyes.
With a kind one, You show Yourself kind. With an upright mighty man, You show Yourself upright.
With a pure one, You show Yourself pure; But with a perverse one, You deal crookedly.
And the humble people You do deliver; But Your eyes are upon the haughty to humble them.
For You are my lamp, O' Havayah; And Havayah does light my darkness.
For by You I run upon a troop; By my Elokim I scale a wall.
Elokim Whose way is perfect; The word of Havayah is tried; He is a shield unto all them that trust in him.
For who is Elokim, save Havayah? And who is a rock, save our Elokim?
Elokim is He who has fortified me with strength; and He looseth perfectly my path.
He makes my feet like hinds; And sets me upon my high places.
He trains my hand for war, so that mine arms do bend a brass bow.
And You have given me the shield of Your salvation; And You have increased Your modesty for me.
You have enlarged my step beneath me; And my ankles have not slipped.
I have pursued my enemies and have destroyed them; Never turning back until they were consumed.
And I have consumed them, and I have crushed them that they cannot rise; Yes, they are fallen under my feet.
For You have girded me with strength for the battle; You have subdued under me those that rose up against me.
And of my enemies You have given me the back of their necks; them that hate me, that I may cut them off.
They looked about, but there was no one to save them; to Havayah, but He answered them not.
Then I ground them as the dust of the earth, as the mud of the streets I did tread upon them, I did stamp them down.
And You have allowed me to escape from the contenders amongst my people; You shall keep me as head of nations; a people whom I have not known serve me.
Strangers lie to me; as soon as their ears hear, they obey me.
The strangers will wilt, and become lame from their bondage.
Havayah lives, and blessed be my Rock; And exalted be Elokim, my rock of salvation.
Elokim who takes vengeance for me; And brings down peoples under me.
And that brings me forth from my enemies; And above those that rise against me, You have lifted me; from the violent man You deliver me.
Therefore I will give thanks to You, O' Havayah, among the nations, and to your name I will sing praises.
He gives great salvation to His king, and He performs kindness to His anointed; to Dovid and to his seed, forevermore.
And these are the last words of Dovid; the saying of Dovid the son of Yishai, and the saying of the man raised on high, the anointed of Elokim of Yackov, And the sweet singer of Yisroel.
The spirit of Havayah spoke in me, And His word was upon my tongue.
Elokim of Yisroel said, concerning me spoke the Rock of Yisroel; 'A ruler over men shall be the righteous, he that rules in the fear of Elokim.
And as the light of the morning the sun shines; a morning without clouds, more than the light that follows the rain that falls upon the grass of the earth.
For my house is not so with Elokim. For an everlasting covenant has He made with me, fully set forth and heeded for all my salvation and all the desire, for He will not sprout forth.
But the wicked are all as thorns thrust away, for they cannot be taken in hand.
But if a man touch them, he should be armed with iron and the staff of a spear; and with fire they shall be utterly burned in their place.
These are the names of the mighty men who Dovid. He who sat in the assembly of the wise, the chief of the three-some, he was Adino the Etzni; against eight hundred slain at one time.

And after him Elazar the son of Dodo the son of an Achochi, among the three mighty men with Dovid, when they risked their lives against the Pelishtim that were gathered there to do battle, while the men of Yisroel had departed.
He rose up and smote the Pelishtim until his hand was weary, and his hand cleaved to the sword; and Havayah performed a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to strip.
And after him Shamah the son of Agei the mountaineer. Now the Pelishtim were gathered together into a troop, and there was a plot of ground full of lentils; and the people fled from the Pelishtim.
But he stationed himself in the midst of the plot and he defended it, and he slew the Pelishtim; and Havayah performed a great victory.
And three of the thirty chiefs went down, and they came in the harvest time to Dovid to the cave of Adulam; and the troop of Pelishtim were encamped in the valley of Refaim.
And Dovid was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Pelishtim was then in Beit Lechem.
And Dovid desired, and he said: "Oh if one would only give me water to drink from the well of Beit Lechem which is by the gate."

And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Pelishtim, and they drew water out of the well of Beit Lechem, that was by the gate, and they carried it and brought it back to Dovid, but he did not care to drink it and he poured it out before Havayah.
And he said: "Be it far from me, O' Havayah, that I should do this; the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives?" And he would not drink it. These performed the three mighty men.
And Avishai, the brother of Yoav, the son of Tzeruyah, was chief of the three. And he roused his sword against three hundred slain at one time, and he had a name among the three.
Of the three he was most honored; and he was their captain; but to the three he did not attain.
And Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, the son of a valiant man great in deeds, of Kabzeel, he smote the two mighty men of Moav, and he went down and smote the lion inside a pit on a snowy day.

And he slew a Mitzri, a man of striking appearance; and in the Mitzri's hand was a spear; and he went down to him with a staff. And he grabbed the spear from the hand of the Mitzri, and slew him with his own spear.
These performed Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, and he had a name among the three mighty men.
Of the thirty he was the most honored, but to the first three he did attain. And Dovid placed him over his following.
Asa'el the brother of Yoav was among the thirty. Elhanan the son of Dodo of Beit Lechem;
Shamah the Charodi, Elika the Charodi;
Cheletz the Palti, Irah, the son of Ikkesh the Teko'i;
Aviezer the Anatoti, Mevunnai the Chushati;
Tzalmon the Achochi, Maharai the Netofati;
Heleb the son of Ba'anah the Netofati, Ittai the son of Rivai of Givah of the children of Binyamin;
Benayahu a Piratoni, Hiddai of Nahale-goash;
Abi-albon the Arvati, Azmavet the Bachurimi;
Eliachba the Sha'alvoni, the sons of Yashen, Yehonatan;
Shamah the Harari, Achiam the son of Sharar the Arari;
Elifelet the son of Achasbai, the son of the Ma'achati, Eliam the son of Achitofel the Giloni;
Chetzrai the Karmeli, Pa'arai the Arvi;
Yigal the son of Natan of Tzovah, Bani the Gadi;
Zelek the Amoni, Nachri the Be'eroti, the armorbearer of Yoav the son of Tzeruyah;
Ira an Yitri, Garev an Yitri;
Uriyah the Chitti; thirty-seven in all.
And again the anger of Havayah was kindled against Yisroel and He moved Dovid against them, saying, "Go count Yisroel and Yehudah."

And the king said to Yoav the captain of the host that was with him, "Go please, to and fro throughout all the tribes of Yisroel, from Dan as far as Be'er Sheva and take census of the people, so that I may know the number of the people."

And Yoav said to the king, "May Havayah your Elokim add to the people a hundredfold of whatsoever they may be, and the eyes of my master, the king may see it; but my master the king, why does he desire such a thing?"

But the word of the king prevailed against Yoav, and against the captains of the host. And Yoav and the captains of the host went out from the presence of the king, to number the people, the Bnei Yisroel.
And they crossed the Yarden, and they camped in Aro'er, to the right of the city that is in the middle of the valley of Gad, and to Ya'zer.
And they came to Gilad, and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi; and they came to Dan to the city of Yaan and round about to Tzidon.
And they came to the stronghold of Tzor, and to all the cities of the Chivim, and of the Kena'anim; and they went out to the South of Yehudah, to Be'er Sheva.
And they had gone to and fro throughout the entire land, and they came at the end of nine months and twenty days Yerushalayim.

And Yoav presented the sum of the number of the people to the king; And Yisroel consisted of eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword; and the men of Yehudah were five hundred thousand men.

And Dovid's heart smote him after he had counted the people. And Dovid said to Havayah: I have sinned greatly in what I have done; and now, 'O Havayah, put aside please, the iniquity of your servant, for I was very foolish!
And Dovid rose up in the morning; and the word of Havayah came to Gad the Prophet, the seer of Dovid, saying:
"Go and speak to Dovid, 'So Havayah says, "Three things I offer you, choose for yourself one of them, and I shall do it to you".

And Gad came to Dovid and he told him, and he said to him, " that seven years of famine in your land shall come upon you? Or three months that you shall flee before your oppressor while he pursues you? Or, that there be three days pestilence in your land? Now know and consider what I shall reply to Him that sent me.
And Dovid said to Gad; "I am greatly oppressed; let us fall now into the hand of Havayah; for His mercies are great; but into the hand of man let me not fall."
So Havayah sent a pestilence upon Yisroel from the morning until the appointed time; And there died of the people from Dan to Be'er Sheva seventy thousand men.

And the angel stretched out his hand toward Yerushalayim to destroy it, and Havayah regretted the evil, and he said to the angel that destroyed among the people, "It is enough; now stay your hand." And the angel of Havayah was by the threshing-floor of Aravnah the Yevusi.

And Dovid said to Havayah when he saw the angel that smote among the people, and he said, "Behold I have sinned, and have acted iniquitously; but these sheep, what have they done? I beg that Your hand be against me, and against my father's house."
And Gad came to Dovid on that day, and said to him, "Go up to erect an altar to Havayah in the threshing-floor of Aravnah the Yevusi."
And Dovid went up according to the word of Gad, as Havayah had commanded.
And Aravnah looked afar and he saw the king and his servants passing on towards him: and Aravnah went out and he bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.

And Aravnah said, "Why has Havayah my king come to his servant?" And Dovid said, "To acquire from you the threshing-floor, in order to build an altar to Havayah, that the plague be stayed from the people."
And Aravnah said to Dovid, "Let my master the king take and offer up what seems good in his eyes; behold the oxen for the burnt-offering and the threshing tools, and the tools of the oxen for wood."
All this Aravnah the king gave to the king. And Aravnah said to the king, "May Havayah your Elokim accept you."

And the king said to Aravnah, "No; for I will only buy it from you at a price; so that I will not offer to Havayah my Elokim burnt-offerings for nothing." And Dovid bought the threshing-floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
And Dovid built there an altar to Havayah, and he offered up burnt-offerings and peace offerings. And Havayah was entreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Yisroel.
